additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional disorder is characterized by one or more persistent delusions lasting at least a month (often many months or years) in the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thought, or marked negative symptoms, and with relatively preserved overall functioning outside the delusional themes. The delusions are fixed false beliefs that remain resistant to clear contradictory evidence and are not better explained by mood episodes, substance use, or another psychotic disorder. Content can involve persecution, jealousy, somatic concerns, grandiosity, or erotomanic ideas, and behavior may be subtly shaped by these beliefs while still appearing outwardly organized. Onset is often insidious in mid to later adulthood, and patients frequently present only after family, employers, or legal systems become involved because the person does not recognize the beliefs as pathological.

patient.stressor: About a year before presentation, Nguyen led a high‑visibility cloud migration project where a series of minor outages drew intense scrutiny from management and online client forums. Around this time, he began fixating on a belief that a competing tech team within the company was covertly sabotaging his code and monitoring his personal accounts, initially channeling the concern into exhaustive log‑checking and late‑night "hardening" work. Over the next nine months, his conviction solidified despite repeated internal audits showing no anomalies, and he started avoiding collaboration, refusing to share documentation, and skipping hackathons and social basketball games to "stay ahead" of the perceived threat. The situation came to a head when HR intervened after he accused a colleague of spying during a sprint review; at the urging of his manager and a trusted cousin from Little Saigon, Nguyen reluctantly agreed to see a psychiatrist as a condition for remaining on the project.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m here because nobody seems to take it seriously that people at work are secretly targeting my projects, even when I show them the evidence.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: No matter how many times IT or my manager say they can't find anything unusual, I can see the pattern in the logs and the timing of the glitches, and I’m convinced this other team has been slipping bad code into my branches and watching my personal accounts to make me look incompetent, so I spend nights double-checking everything because I know they’re still at it even if everyone else refuses to see it.

add_requirements.preserved_functioning_outside_delusion: Outside of trying to protect my projects from that other team, I still handle my regular tickets, help junior devs debug their code, pay my bills on time, and meet up with my cousin for pho on weekends like I always have.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I’m constantly on guard about my coworkers sabotaging me, I’ve pulled back from team events and late-night basketball, and HR has warned me that my accusations in meetings are putting my position on the project at risk.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about nine months now, ever since that big cloud migration last year when the outages happened and I first became convinced the other team was targeting me.
